newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Egypt responsible to locate Israeli.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Egypt responsible to locate Israeli.

text.p: Israel said on Monday it was Egypt's responsibility to help find an Israeli man abducted outside his Cairo area hotel.

"We are doing everything, as is our elementary obligation as a state to look after a citizen who has disappeared. It is the responsibility of Egypt to do everything to give us not only information but to return him to us," Foreign Minister David Levy told Israel's Channel One television.
Levy will take up the case while in Cairo on Tuesday for a Middle East economic conference, his office said.

Israel's charge d'affaires in Egypt, Jacob Gil, told Reuters Azam Azam, who had been working at a Cairo textile factory, was abducted when he returned to the Baron Hotel in the suburb of Medinet Nasr last Wednesday.

"His father says people from security took him away. We checked this at a very high level and they know nothing about it. They have no reason not to tell us the truth," he said, adding he had asked to meet Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi.
Azam, in his late 30s, was chief mechanic at the factory.

An official at the Tefron company, the Israeli owner, said witnesses saw about 10 well-dressed people, some with walkie-talkies, approach Azam at the entrance to the hotel as he got out of a cab. They asked a few questions and demanded to see his identification before taking him away.
Egypt's interior ministry said it had no information on the case. Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel.
